title: Browserless provider admission and human-interaction incident

signals.observation: WSL restart replaced the surfpath namespace generation; Browserless was subsequently rebound to the current exterior-anchor authority.
The localhost operator bridge successfully carried HTTP and CDP WebSocket traffic after the manual parked session was removed.
Production Browserless launch was observed with userDataDir=/data; missing persistent profile binding is not supported as the current failure explanation.

Browserless OSS 2.56.0 session viewer routes an existing page to DevTools Inspector while its interactive Runner creates a new browser session; this does not satisfy exact parked-session human interaction.
ChatGPT provider preflight returned CHALLENGE_GATED with providerEffectAttempted=false and no composer fill or SEND.
A fresh production Browserless connection caused the current Browserless bearer token to appear in the carrier system journal.

hypotheses.statement: The current provider failure is caused by a broken localhost HTTP/WebSocket bridge.
hypotheses.falsifier: Release the manual diagnostic holder and establish about:blank CDP connections through both root and /chromium operator bridge endpoints.

hypotheses.statement: The current provider failure is caused by Browserless not using the persistent profile.
hypotheses.falsifier: Run the production connection endpoint inside the bound network namespace and observe the browser launch user-data-dir.

hypotheses.statement: The self-hosted Browserless Debugger can serve as an exact-session interactive human handoff for a parked Browserless session.
hypotheses.falsifier: Inspect Browserless 2.56.0 debugger session-viewer and Runner implementations and verify whether input is attached to the existing tracked session.

hypotheses.statement: Browserless bearer-token logging is a current local security defect.
hypotheses.falsifier: Execute a fresh production Browserless connection after logging hardening and prove the current bearer token is absent from new journal entries.

hypotheses.statement: The exact reason the external provider presented a challenge at this time is known.
hypotheses.falsifier: Obtain provider-authoritative evidence linking the challenge to one specific client condition rather than temporal correlation.

explicitUnknowns: The provider-authoritative reason for the challenge is unavailable.
A compliant exact-session human interaction transport is not yet integrated into the current self-hosted Browserless path.
notes: Founding Engineer E2E Autonomous Incident Closure case. Provider challenge handling must not bypass or evade provider controls; only the irreducible account-owner action may escalate to the owner.
